hints: Use the gradient between the two given points, then rearrange the resulting equation to make $b$ the subject.
walkthrough:
Use the gradient formula between $A(-1, 1)$ and $P(a, b)$:
$$m_{AP} = \frac{b - 1}{a - (-1)} = \frac{b - 1}{a + 1} = 2$$

Rearrange to express $b$ explicitly in terms of $a$:
$$b - 1 = 2(a + 1) = 2a + 2 \implies b = 2a + 3$$

Calculate the square of the distance between $A(-1, 1)$ and $B(10, -1)$:
$$AB^2 = (10 - (-1))^2 + (-1 - 1)^2 = 11^2 + (-2)^2 = 121 + 4 = 125$$

Set $AP^2 = AB^2 = 125$ using the distance formula for $P(a, b)$:
$$(a + 1)^2 + (b - 1)^2 = 125$$

Substitute $b - 1 = 2(a + 1)$ into the distance equation:
$$(a + 1)^2 + [2(a + 1)]^2 = 125 \implies (a + 1)^2 + 4(a + 1)^2 = 125$$
$$5(a + 1)^2 = 125 \implies (a + 1)^2 = 25$$
$$a + 1 = 5 \implies a = 4 \quad \text{or} \quad a + 1 = -5 \implies a = -6$$

Calculate the corresponding values of $b = 2a + 3$:
$$\text{For } a = 4: \quad b = 2(4) + 3 = 11 \implies (4, 11)$$
$$\text{For } a = -6: \quad b = 2(-6) + 3 = -9 \implies (-6, -9)$$
$$\text{Possible coordinates of } P: \quad (4, 11) \quad \text{and} \quad (-6, -9)$$
